title: Ops velocity and SLO delta notes — weekly prep
content:
Weekly SRE ops sync prep - quick scratchpad

Date: 2026-04-21 (weekly ops sync)
Owner: Asha Patel (notes + follow-ups)
Attendees (expected): Diego R., Priya N., Sam L., oncall rotation + infra rep

Meeting goals (what I want out of this):
- Surface SLO drift and decide if we should burn/stop pages or throttle routes.
- Review paging trends last 7/30 days and identify any emerging clusters.
- Quick root cause & follow-up status for the top 2 incidents (INC-453, INC-467).
- Confirm rollout windows for upcoming kernel/driver patch that may impact GPU pool N+1.
- Capture action items with owners and due dates; flag anything that needs EM/manager escalation.

Agenda (rough order):
1) Quick standup (1m each): noise, scheduled maintenance, holidays impacting oncall.
2) SLO snapshot + error budget status (5m) — focus on latency SLOs for hosted API routes and kv-cache tail latencies.
3) Paging trends (10m) — heatmap of pages by service, severity, flapping pages.
4) Incident deep-dive(s) (15m) — INC-453 summary + owner update, high-level RCA for INC-467 follow-ups.
5) Upcoming infra changes & risk window (5m) — scheduled kernel/drivers + Dedicated capacity burst test.
6) Action items + owners (3m).

Prep notes / data to have handy:
- SLO dashboard link: Confluence SLO dashboard (linked above) — pull 7d/30d comparisons.
- Error budget burn: hosting api: 99.9 p99 latency — current 7d burn = 8.6% (target threshold 10%).
- KV-cache tail latency: p99 has increased from 120ms -> 380ms over 7 days for heavy-prefix workloads (region: us-west2).
- Pager counts: last 7 days: total pages = 42 (up from 28 previous week). Top sources: kv-cache (12), router-proxy (9), model-runtime OOMs (7).
- Flapping signature: 3 recurring pages for kv-cache (same service, different hosts) -> possible noisy host-level metric or flaky network.

Incident summaries (short):
- INC-453 (2026-04-17) 
  - Symptom: 5xx spike for hosted API endpoint /v1/generate during high batching window.
  - Root cause (current hypothesis): memory pressure + suboptimal kv-cache eviction caused cascading GC pauses on model hosts, resulting in request timeouts and 502s.
  - What we did: rolled back the recent kv-cache tuning config (quantile threshold change), scaled up eviction worker count, drained 3 unhealthy hosts.
  - Status: mitigation applied, monitoring steady. Owner: Priya N. (SRE). Linked ticket: INC-453.
  - Open questions: need deeper profiling of kv-cache eviction algorithm under load; consider circuit-breaker for model-runtime calls.

- INC-467 (2026-04-19) 
  - Symptom: intermittent pod OOMs in model-runtime canaries after a new runtime PR (PR#289) landed.
  - Action taken: reverted PR on canary pool, re-run stress harness, observed reduced OOMs. Owner: Diego R.
  - Status: in-progress RCA; likely memory regression in quantization path.
  - Follow-up: create smaller reproducer + heap dump capture; triage with runtime team.

Paging trends & hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: kv-cache config change + peaky traffic patterns -> increased p99 latency and more pages. Need to throttle background eviction during production peak.
- Hypothesis B: the recent kernel/driver mismatch on some Dedicated hosts increased GC pause variance. Confirm driver versions across pool.
- Hypothesis C: alert thresholds tuned for earlier baseline; we should consider raising noisy-but-low-impact alerts to warning only (reduce pager noise).

Proposed small-scope mitigations to discuss in sync (fast wins):
- Add short-lived suppression for non-actionable kv-cache alerts during peak batch windows (owner: Priya; due: 2026-04-23).
- Add a per-host healthcheck that quarantines hosts with >5 evictions/minute (owner: Diego; due: 2026-04-24).
- Roll forward small probe that dumps heap on OOM to a secure S3 path for faster triage (owner: Sam; due: 2026-04-22).

Longer follow-ups (RCA workstreams):
- Deep dive on kv-cache eviction algorithm under production tail workloads — pair SRE + runtime (owner: Priya + runtime eng; ticket: SRE-2145; ETA: 2026-05-07).
- Model-runtime quantization memory regression analysis and fix (owner: runtime eng; link PR#289; ETA: 2026-05-05).
- Review alerting noise across SLOs and produce a 'noise reduction' plan (owner: Asha; checklist doc to be created; ETA: 2026-05-01).

Action items (explicit):
- A1) Priya: implement suppression window for kv-cache noisy alerts during heavy-batch periods. Add to PagerDuty rule and doc changes. Due 2026-04-23. Jira/PD note: INC-453 follow-up.
- A2) Diego: add host-level quarantine rule for >5 evictions/min; mock in staging and run for 48h. Due 2026-04-24. Ticket: infra-eviction-quarantine-2026.
- A3) Sam: enable heap-dump-on-OOM for canary pool and upload to secure bucket; test retrieval flow for engineers. Due 2026-04-22.
- A4) Asha: draft alert noise reduction plan and runbook updates; share with SRE and Console/Observability PMs. Due 2026-05-01. Confluence draft link will be added.
- A5) Priya + runtime eng: schedule 90m RCA session for kv-cache eviction with traffic replay data. Due 2026-04-29. Ticket: SRE-2145.

Notes-to-self / meeting prompts:
- Ask infra: can we get a simple mapping of driver/kernel versions across dedicated pools? (esp us-west2, us-east1)
- Should we consider lowering the frequency of p99-based alerts and rely more on error budget velocity alerts? Bring metrics examples.
- Check if any customer-visible SLAs were impacted last week — flag to CS if so.

Follow-ups after meeting (placeholders):
- If Priya confirms suppression worked, update runbooks and close part of INC-453.
- If heap-dump captures show reproducible path, open a runtime PR for memory fixes and link to INC-467.

Misc scratch items (notes to self):
- Pull the last 3 weeks of batch distribution histograms before sync.
- Remind Diego to include canary replay rate in next Monday's test window.
- Quick check: Dedicated autoscale burst config will be tested 2026-04-28 — ensure we don't run heavy jobs that day.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to tidy agenda + publish to PD channel after quick review.

-- Asha
